title: Omni Documents are the Artifact's residual container for everything the Primitive taxonomy does not cover
content:
A.6.1.1.7.3 defines the Omni Documents as covering "Osero's strategic intent and operational processes relating to infrastructure inherited from Sky Core, activities unrelated to Sky Primitives, or activities spanning multiple Sky Primitives."

The three cases are distinct failures of the Primitive model, and naming all three is an admission worth noting. Some of what an Agent does predates the Primitive framework (inherited Sky Core infrastructure); some falls outside it entirely; and some cuts across Primitive boundaries, so filing it under any single Primitive would be arbitrary.

Every classification scheme applied to real activity needs a residual bucket. The design question is whether the bucket is acknowledged or improvised, and the Atlas chooses acknowledged: Omni Documents sit at the same structural level as the entire Sky Primitives section (A.6.1.1.7.2), not tucked inside it.

The risk is drift. A residual category with no membership criteria beyond "doesn't fit" can absorb material that should have driven a new Primitive or an extension of an existing one — and content in Omni Documents is not covered by the Hub/Instance machinery that makes Primitive usage auditable. There is no Global Activation Status or Invocation record for an Omni Document.

That makes the section's contents the part of the Artifact with the least structural discipline, which is why it is notable that Osero's undefined emergency protocols and its Ecosystem Accord both live there.
description: They hold inherited Sky Core infrastructure, activity unrelated to any Primitive, and activity spanning several — conceding the Primitive set is not exhaustive.
